OpenBible's point for Abarim is Mount Nebo (Jabal al Naba), from OpenStreetMap. Point: Pleiades 563265622 (Nebo), the mean of its locations not based on OpenStreetMap (decision 84): one, the imagery location of the summit. Deut.32.49 sends Moses up the Abarim Range to Mount Nebo.

Khirbet el-Mahalib on the Lebanese coast, about 6 km north of Tyre and 2 km south of the Litani mouth (Aharoni). Sennacherib's 701 BC account lists Mahalliba between Zarephath and Ushu (mainland Tyre), and the Septuagint reads Meheleb in Josh.19.29. Confidence fairly good: the name and the Assyrian itinerary agree. Alternative: Gush Halab (Giscala), which fits a list of Phoenician coastal towns poorly. Point approximate, not from OpenStreetMap; check on a map. Owner's research, 2026-10-22.
No point. Helbah is a possible variant of Ahlab (place:ahlab_35) rather than a separate site; another source says it has not been recovered, so no point of its own. Owner's research, 2026-10-22.

The same site as Ahlab (place:ahlab_35), Khirbet el-Mahalib: Sennacherib's Mahalliba and the Septuagint's Meheleb fit Josh.19.29. Point approximate, not from OpenStreetMap; check on a map. Owner's research, 2026-10-22.

The rock of Etam at Araq Ismain, about 2.5 miles (4 km) east south east of Zorah, in Samson's home ground in the Shephelah near Beth Shemesh; a Byzantine cave church tradition links it to Samson (late tradition only). Confidence moderate. Alternative: Khirbet el-Khokh near Artas, which confuses the rock with the town of Etam in Judah; the Etam of 1Chr.4.32 is a third place. Point derived, not copied: 4 km on a bearing of 112.5 degrees from Tel Tzora (Zorah), Wikidata Q3546415 (31.773992, 34.985289); OpenBible's point for Araq Ismain is an OpenStreetMap node and is not used. Owner's research and review, 2026-10-22.

Khirbet Hazzur, a little east of Nebi Samwil, north west of Jerusalem, beside Ramah and Gittaim in the Benjaminite list. The best supported of these places. Not Hazor-hadattah (Josh.15.25) or the northern Hazor. Point derived, not copied, and approximate: 1 km east of Nabi Samwil, Wikidata Q3532567 (31.832733, 35.180150), since the sources give no distance; OpenBible's point for Khirbet Hazzur is an OpenStreetMap node and is not used. Owner's research and review, 2026-10-22.

The land around Pethor (Pitru, on the west bank of the Euphrates a few miles south of Carchemish, near the Sajur), roughly 36.5 N, 38 E; this reading is likelier but not certain (some versions read the land of the sons of Ammon, in Transjordan). No point: better shown as a path. The Wadi Malaki, a gorge about 8 miles north east of Maon that cannot be crossed without a long detour; one dictionary gives 31 27 N, 35 14 E. Other scholars say the place is unknown; Masada is too far from Maon. Owner's research, 2026-10-22.

No point: a district of Gadite pasturelands east of the Jordan, beside Gilead and Bashan (roughly the plateau of northern Gilead and southern Bashan), not the coastal plain. Any point would be false precision. Owner's research, 2026-10-22.

No point: a watercourse near Susa (the Greeks' Eulaeus) that scholars place on the eastern branch of the Karkheh, on the Coprates tributary of the Karun, or on a canal linking the two; the rivers of this plain moved, so a point would be a guess. Better shown as a region between the Karkheh and the Karun. Owner's research, 2026-10-22.

The Valley of Aven is usually identified with the Beqaa Valley; Baalbek stands for the valley. Point: GeoNames 277130 (Baalbek), the name match that the country rule of decision 167 drops because the Places that share its Verses lie in Syria and Iraq. Owner's review, 2026-10-22.
